dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Hehe... Animal noggins are so adorable...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Looking for desert foxes?

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Ah, hello there. Judging by your attire, you must be the Traveler, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Hehe, of course I know you! You're a real celebrity — everyone's heard at least a little about you.

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Your friends, Mr. Cyno and Mr. Tighnari, are really famous themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: I was just looking for a way to see Desert Foxes more often. They're so cute, I can't help wanting to see them more! If only there was some way to make them less skittish around me, so I could touch their tails and...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I didn't know you liked them so much.

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: It's not just them — all animals fascinate me! I suppose that it's an occupational hazard, though. After all, King Deshret's Seven Pillars are all animal-associated one way or the other, right?

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: As I read these books, I slowly developed a deep interest in animals...

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: The Goat King, Crocodile King, Ibis King... Large animals all! And their heads...

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Yup, yup... So cute...

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Animals just have such adorable heads!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: They all sound pretty famous.

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: That's right. The associated literature indicates that the Dragon King, the supreme spirit Apep, was alone amongst the Seven Pillars in not appearing in person.

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Of the remaining six, these were most important: The Goat King Heryshaf, Minister of Ministers, the Crocodile King Sobek, Captain of Captains, the Ibis King Thoth, Scribe of Scribes...

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: And Hermanubis, greatest of sages.

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: As for the other two, Bennu Most-Radiant and Shesepankh Most-Holy, the texts claim that they refer more to "human souls" and "Jinni."

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Speaking of Jinni, it's just a shame that I was born this late. I'd love to have seen a legendary being like that in the flesh.

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Err, sorry, I said that out loud, didn't I?

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: I'd originally intended to just share some ancient knowledge — I've always loved these "names and titles" bridging segments in books! Especially when someone starts to rattle theirs off...

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: And the best titles are slightly on the long side.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks for the lesson!

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Oh, come now, don't say that.

dialogues.speaker: Asenath
dialogues.text: Have you been coming around often lately? We should go see some Desert Foxes together if you've got the time — and some other animals too!
